messages:
nina: FYI — we had a near-miss today: sustained GPU saturation during a tenants rerank batch and the system immediately started 429ing. We need a less binary degrade path.
oscar: oof. do we know what admission rule fired? quick logs?
frank: admission decided to enforce hard throttle when queue_time_ms > 1500 for more than 10s. It was intended as safety but it was too aggressive for mixed workloads.
li: proposal sketch: 1) detect util spike (util > 85% for 15s), 2) apply per-route soft-queueing (max 50ms extra), 3) fall back to variant downgrade (v2 -> v2-small) for non-chat routes, 4) sample soft-shed responses, 5) hard 429 only after queue + downgrade fail.
nina: agree on order. also add hysteresis: require spike to persist for 3 buckets (15s) and then require <70% for 30s to rollback. avoids flapping.
oscar: how do we avoid growing in-memory queues during spikes? queueing hurts memory. maybe use a short-lived edge buffer + token-bucket refill into workers rather than in-worker queues.
li: yep, token-bucket on ingress. queue only for route-level fast window (<= 100 requests). otherwise backpressure with 202 Accept? (for async)
frank: gotta be careful with semantics. returning 202 changes app semantics. better to keep sync but fail fast with a header explaining degrade. e.g. `x-redwood-degrade: stage=queue, slot=32/50, profile=graceful-v1`.
oscar: quality concerns: downgrading model will change output. we need a tiny canary check — 10 synthetic prompts evaluated on candidate variant in <50ms to ensure gross regressions aren't triggered. if canary fails, skip variant and increase queue window.
li: canary evaluator should be local-lightweight (no KV warmup) and use per-tenant prompt subset. store per-tenant canary set in platform.
nina: abuse detection interplay: separate throttle for suspected abuse. If abuse_score > 0.8, skip graceful steps and go to probation. But must log why to console and notify CS.
oscar: product asks for opt-in: customers can choose `degrade_preference: [quality, latency, drop]` in tenant settings. default = latency (prefer to keep quality).
frank: runtime changes: emit structured event `degrade_event` to tracing (fields: tenant_id, route, stage, reason, variant_before, variant_after, sample_prompt_id). Console can surface a timeline.
li: infra: need mem-safe limiters. implement a bounded ring buffer on ingress + reservoir token buckets per-route. Also expose telemetry for queue depth percentiles.
oscar: test plan: synthetic runner that mixes 60% chat, 30% rerank, 10% embeddings with spikes and can toggle `degrade_profile`. Measure p50/p95/p99, quality BLEU-like delta on canary set, and billing delta.
nina: billing: when variant downgraded, tag usage with actual variant_id and bill accordingly. show in cost breakdown so customers see why unit price changed.
frank: ops runbook snippet: `#force-disable-graceful
curl -X POST /internal/tenants/xyz/degrade_lock -d '{"lock":true}'` then `make drain-tenant TENANT=xyz` — keep in runbook.
li: rollout: start internal tenants, then beta customers, then global. Add progressive ramping: apply to 10% of low-priority tenants for 5m, evaluate, then widen.
oscar: edge case: private deployments. expose `degrade_mode=allowed|disallowed` so on-prem can opt out of automatic variant changes and prefer explicit 429s.
frank: open question: should we expose a public API for customers to control `degrade_profile_id` programmatically? seems useful for partners.
nina: let's capture decisions and options in RFC. action owners: oscar -> RFC draft; li -> ingress token-bucket prototype; frank -> telemetry/event schema + header; nina -> test harness and runbook updates.
ops-bot: created ticket INF-6001: "Graceful degrade + hysteresis + ingress buffer RFC" assigned eng-platform. :white_check_mark:
oscar: i'll post RFC in 72h.
li: will prototype token-bucket this week.
frank: ill draft the event shape and add console sketch.
nina: thanks all. small goal: avoid hard 429s as first resort next quarter. :thumbsup:
